title: Microsoft Teams: improvements to the activity in other accounts and orgs panel
summary: The roadmap facts and documented panel behaviour check out, including the device-policy key flagged by the pre-check. The claim that users previously had to switch tenants to see other tenants' activity is unsubstantiated; the briefing should also qualify the notification count, acknowledge the general Teams licence requirement and recommend preparing communications.

claims.where: controls[1].ui
claims.claim: No admin-centre UI for the desktop RestrictTeamsSignInToAccountsFromTenantList device policy is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'RestrictTeamsSignInToAccountsFromTenantList admin center UI policy'; opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/sign-in-teams. It documents desktop GPO/MDM, registry and plist configuration, not an admin-centre path for this policy.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The desktop device policy restricts first and additional account sign-ins to accounts homed in Microsoft Entra tenants in its allow list.
claims.quote: When this policy is configured on a device, users can only sign in with accounts homed in a Microsoft Entra tenant that's included in the "Tenant Allow List" defined in the policy. The policy applies to all sign-ins, including first and additional accounts.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The desktop sign-in policy is deployed through device management such as MDM or GPO.
claims.quote: The policies can be set via usual Device Management solutions such as MDM (Mobile Device Management) or GPO (Group Policy Object).

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The sign-in policy does not stop users being invited as guests in other tenants or switching to those guest tenants.
claims.quote: The policy only restricts sign-ins. It does not restrict the ability for users to be invited as a guest in other Microsoft Entra tenants, or switch to those other tenants (where users have been invited as a guest).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The panel uses accounts or organisations the user is already signed in to.
claims.quote: Appears in the Teams sidebar when you’re signed into multiple accounts or organizations. Click on your profile picture, at the top right corner in Teams, to view all your accounts and organizations that you are signed in with.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly specified whether the panel lists guest tenants.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams activity panel guest'; 'Activity in other accounts and orgs license pricing meter guest'. Opened activity-in-other-accounts-orgs and sign-in-teams; read guest-access search excerpt. None explicitly specifies guest-tenant inclusion in this panel.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Learn describes notification display and opening on a user click, not automated actions by the panel.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Activity in other accounts and orgs admin setting disable PowerShell Graph'; opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/activity-in-other-accounts-orgs. Its How it works, Interacting with activity notifications and Pinning Tenants sections describe no automated action.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is recorded as unknown because Microsoft has not published a feature-specific licence requirement.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included' and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Replace the licensing explanation with 'Manage Teams licenses states that, except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organisation needs a Teams licence to use Teams. No panel-specific licence requirement is published.' In the summary, replace 'any licence' with 'a panel-specific licence requirement'; narrow the licensing question and rationale to panel-specific licensing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The panel's Learn page names no licence requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Activity in other accounts and orgs license pricing meter guest'; 'Teams activity panel license'. Opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/activity-in-other-accounts-orgs; its complete text names no licence requirement.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No panel-specific meter, charge or price is published in the documentation checked.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Activity in other accounts and orgs license pricing meter guest'; 'Teams activity panel license'. Opened activity-in-other-accounts-orgs; read user-access and Teams add-on licenses search excerpts. No panel-specific meter, price or charge is documented.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The roadmap record gives no pricing.
claims.quote: Stay up-to-date with what's happening in your other accounts and organizations with the 'Activity in Other Accounts and Orgs' panel. Preview and open chats, channels, and other activity in other accounts and orgs from your main Teams window, without switching tenants.

claims.where: Scope: Rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described the improvements' rollout mechanics or additional prerequisites.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Activity in other accounts and orgs improvements default rollout prerequisites January 2027'; opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/activity-in-other-accounts-orgs and read roadmap record. Neither gives the improvements' rollout mechanics or additional prerequisites.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Before this change, users could see another tenant's activity only after switching tenants.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams other accounts organizations notifications before switching tenants multitenant organizations'; opened activity-in-other-accounts-orgs and read Plan for multitenant organizations search excerpts. Neither establishes that historical restriction.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with 'For a service owner, the panel brings another tenant's activity notifications together in the main Teams window.' Remove 'rather than only after switching tenants'.

claims.where: front matter: action; summary; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The review action rating fits improvements to an existing interface for which the briefing recommends preparing users and the help desk before rollout.
claims.quote: action: "review"; 'tell them the panel and its notification previews are coming'; 'Brief the help desk on the 10-notification limit'.
claims.fix: Set action to 'prepare' and replace 'admins should review it' in the summary with 'admins should prepare user communications'. The standard assigns prepare to improvements or redesigns of existing behaviour needing communication, even with an unknown default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Viewing notifications does not mark them read; they clear when clicked in the panel or viewed in the tenant's main Activity app.
claims.quote: Viewing activity notifications in the panel doesn’t mark items as read; they clear when clicked in the panel or viewed in that tenant’s main Activity app.
